query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

levers.lever: Machine Learning Potential (MLP) with active learning
levers.principle: Improves reference–target phase-space overlap by learning the complex potential energy surface of high-entropy alloys from ab initio data, reducing the need for explicit atomic configurations in EAM references. Key parameters: training dataset size (10,000 to 100,000 configurations), active learning cycle count (5 to 20), and MLP model complexity (2 to 5 hidden layers). Applicable composition range: 3 to 6 principal elements, temperature range: 0.8 to 1.2 times the melting temperature. Supporting evidence: successful application of MLP in elemental and binary systems. Decisive free-energy benchmark: prediction of the solid-liquid phase transition temperature within 50 K of experimental values.

levers.lever: Neural Network Potential (NNP) with transfer learning
levers.principle: Enhances the representation of atomic configurations by leveraging pre-trained neural networks and fine-tuning them on high-entropy alloy datasets, thereby improving the transferability of EAM references. Key parameters: pre-training dataset size (50,000 to 500,000 configurations), fine-tuning dataset size (1,000 to 10,000 configurations), and NNP model complexity (3 to 6 hidden layers). Applicable composition range: 4 to 8 principal elements, temperature range: 0.7 to 1.1 times the melting temperature. Supporting evidence: successful application of NNP in binary and ternary systems. Decisive free-energy benchmark: prediction of the liquidus temperature within 100 K of experimental values.

levers.lever: Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP) with Bayesian optimization
levers.principle: Optimizes the representation of atomic configurations by using Bayesian optimization to select the most relevant configurations for inclusion in the GAP model, reducing the computational cost and improving the accuracy. Key parameters: number of Bayesian optimization iterations (10 to 50), GAP model complexity (2 to 5 kernel functions), and configuration selection threshold (0.1 to 0.5). Applicable composition range: 3 to 6 principal elements, temperature range: 0.8 to 1.2 times the melting temperature. Supporting evidence: successful application of GAP in elemental and binary systems. Decisive free-energy benchmark: prediction of the solid-liquid phase transition entropy within 10% of experimental values.

levers.lever: Moment Tensor Potential (MTP) with genetic algorithm optimization
levers.principle: Improves the representation of atomic configurations by using a genetic algorithm to optimize the MTP model parameters, allowing for a more accurate description of the complex interactions in high-entropy alloys. Key parameters: number of genetic algorithm generations (10 to 50), population size (100 to 1000), and MTP model complexity (2 to 5 moment tensor orders). Applicable composition range: 4 to 8 principal elements, temperature range: 0.7 to 1.1 times the melting temperature. Supporting evidence: successful application of MTP in binary and ternary systems. Decisive free-energy benchmark: prediction of the liquidus temperature within 150 K of experimental values.
